highlights.description: An open JSON format for a cloud service's self-attested security documents, with typed facts stated once and claims that say how true they are
`secdocs lint` reports what is invalid or still to be done, by rule ID and JSON path
`secdocs render` and `secdocs export` publish Markdown and JSON from one audience-filtered view, so NDA and internal content cannot leak
Builds only on sources that allow free commercial reuse: NIST SP 800-53, FedRAMP's 2026 rules and RFC 9116

added.description: `spec` package: `DocumentSet` with shared fact groups and six typed documents (security overview, security response, subprocessors, data handling, incident response, availability) plus custom documents
Claims with status, verification level, visibility, gaps, justifications, evidence and control references
Placeholders such as `{{org.name}}` and `{{doc.security-response}}` in prose
`spec.Load` and `spec.Scaffold` for reading a set and starting one where every claim is todo
JSON Schema generated from the Go types and embedded as `schema.JSON`
`lint` package: error, warning and info rules for structure, status, gaps, dates, reviews, placeholders, control ID formats and consistency between facts
`render` package: Markdown per document with an index, draft mode, gap handling, YAML front matter and a combined file for Pandoc
`render.ExportJSON`: the machine-readable copy of the rendered view, refusing unassessed claims unless in draft
`render.SecurityTxt`: an RFC 9116 security.txt from the security-response document

tests.description: Unit, golden-file and leak tests over a complete fictional example set, Example Notes

documentation.description: README with usage, the document set and library use
Sources and licensing guide: which frameworks may be embedded and which are named by ID only
